card: Fixes a latent bug in script decompression where oversized scripts append OP_RETURN to the target script buffer instead of replacing it. If the destination script buffer is reused and contains an unfinished data push, the appended opcode is treated as data, leaving the output spendable. The author notes that oversized scripts are currently excluded from the UTXO set so the issue appears latent, but it could affect malformed stored records decoded into a reused destination buffer.
evidence: Author description: "The oversized-script fallback appends OP_RETURN to the destination instead of replacing it. If the destination already contains an unfinished push, the appended byte becomes pushed data and the result can remain spendable."

Author notes the flaw appears latent in practice: "This predates that PR and appears latent because oversized outputs are excluded from the UTXO set, but it could affect malformed stored records decoded into a reused destination."
problem: When decoding an oversized compressed script into an existing script buffer that already contains an incomplete data push, appending OP_RETURN incorporates the byte into the pushed data instead of terminating the script, leaving the resulting script potentially spendable.

risk.why: Altering script decompression logic used by UTXO serialization could cause chainstate database corruption or validation discrepancies if handled improperly.

scope_notes: Very small patch (+14/-1) spanning the script compressor and a compressor unit test.
summary: Fix oversized script decompression so that it overwrites the destination buffer with an OP_RETURN script rather than appending to it. It also adds a unit test verifying that decoding into a reused script with an unfinished push produces an unspendable script.
